goal: Add a nullable blocked_requires_json column to the lifecycles row (SQLite + Postgres schemas, Lifecycle dataclass, and all store INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT paths) that round-trips through every backend.

references: src/flywheel/lifecycle.py:90-103 -- Lifecycle dataclass: add blocked_requires_json: str | None = None as a new nullable field, default None
src/flywheel/_schema/persistence-schema.sql:32-45 -- lifecycles CREATE TABLE that gains a `blocked_requires_json TEXT` column (nullable, no DEFAULT clause -- TEXT NULL is the SQLite default)
src/flywheel/_schema/persistence-schema-postgres.sql:44-57 -- mirror the same change for the Postgres CREATE TABLE
src/flywheel/store_sqlite.py:206-234 -- INSERT INTO lifecycles -- add the column to the column list and the VALUES tuple
src/flywheel/store_sqlite.py:236-287 -- UPDATE lifecycles SET ... -- add the column to the SET list and the params tuple so clearing to NULL works
src/flywheel/store_sqlite.py:289-316 -- SELECT FROM lifecycles -- add the column to the projection and populate Lifecycle.blocked_requires_json (NULL -> None)
src/flywheel/store_postgres.py:286-360 -- mirror INSERT, UPDATE, and SELECT changes for the Postgres backend
src/flywheel/store_memory.py:49-65 -- _clone_lifecycle_row helper that must propagate the new field

Parked branch flywheel/04-recoverable-blocked-lifecycles/envelope-blocked-requires (commit e9587a0) did NOT touch lifecycle/schema/stores, so there is no prior reference implementation for this task -- the spec is the source of truth.
constraints: The new column is `blocked_requires_json TEXT` (nullable) in SQLite and `blocked_requires_json TEXT` (nullable) in Postgres. No CHECK constraint, no index, no DEFAULT clause -- NULL is the default. Mirror the same column-name spelling in both schemas exactly.

Lifecycle gains `blocked_requires_json: str | None = None`. The harness owns serialization/deserialization in a later task; this module stores the value verbatim. Do NOT import json into flywheel.lifecycle -- the existing purity test (tests/test_lifecycle_module_purity.py) must continue to pass unchanged.

All three stores (SqliteStore, PostgresStore, InMemoryStore) must round-trip the value: create_lifecycle persists it, update_lifecycle updates it (including setting it back to NULL), load_lifecycle returns it. A SELECT * projection alone is not enough -- explicitly include the column in the hand-written SELECT lists.

Round-trip tests in tests/test_store_sqlite.py, tests/test_store_postgres.py, and tests/test_store_memory.py: persist a Lifecycle with blocked_requires_json set to a non-empty JSON string, reload, assert equality; persist a Lifecycle with blocked_requires_json=None, reload, assert it stays None; update an existing row from a non-None value back to None, reload, assert clearing worked.
Extend tests/test_store_contract.py (the shared contract test) so the round-trip assertion runs against every backend uniformly -- this prevents one store from drifting.

Do NOT bump CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION in src/flywheel/store_protocols.py for this task -- bumping it forces every dev DB to be recreated and the spec's Non-Functional Requirements explicitly accept the NULL-on-existing-rows back-compat path. The next harness task can bump it if appropriate, but for THIS task the existing schema_version=2 still applies because adding a nullable column without a DEFAULT is a backward-compatible read change (the SELECT projection still resolves on databases that already have the column from a fresh install, and brand-new DBs get the column from the CREATE TABLE). Old databases lacking the column will fail any SELECT that names it -- this is acceptable per the spec's 'existing dev DBs can be wiped' tradeoff (see spec 00002 Non-Functional Requirements).
Do NOT add migration scripts. New columns on existing rows are NULL by default; the spec explicitly accepts this back-compat path.
Do NOT add any harness or workflow logic in this task. The harness wiring (populating the column on block, clearing on -> READY) lives in the next task.
After editing Python, run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py file you touch and fix all Pylance errors before reporting verify -- treat them as build failures (see CLAUDE.md).
Commit the change with a Conventional Commits message (e.g. 'feat:' or 'refactor:') before reporting verify.
non_goals: Do not import json into flywheel.lifecycle; do not add helpers that parse the column. Serialization is the harness's job.
Do not change any other column on lifecycles or any other table.
Do not change the Lifecycle.transition_to logic in this task -- clearing on -> READY belongs to the harness task.
Do not edit docs in this task; documentation updates ride with the harness task that defines the behavior.
Do not bump CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION. (See constraint above.)
edge_cases: load_lifecycle must default the field to None when the stored value is SQL NULL -- do not coerce NULL to empty string.
_clone_lifecycle_row in store_memory.py must propagate blocked_requires_json, otherwise the in-memory store will silently drop it across create/update/load.
Postgres TEXT vs JSONB: use TEXT (matching SQLite). The harness will serialize/deserialize JSON itself; treating the column as opaque text keeps the protocol uniform.

If a brand-new SqliteStore is created against an existing DB file with schema_version=2 but no blocked_requires_json column, the next INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT will fail with `no such column`. Document in the test plan that this is expected -- developers wipe .workflow/flywheel.sqlite to pick up the column. The schema_version bump that would make this loud is intentionally deferred (see constraints).
